燃え爛れる町の中で、ただ一人生き残れた責任を追い続けた。

pages.en:
It happened ten years ago.

Ever since I alone survived that burning, festering city, I have pursued the responsibility of survival.
pages.mirrorMoon:
It all happened ten years ago.
I kept pursuing the responsibility for being the only survivor in the fire.

救われなかった人たちに胸を張れるように使われ続け、それを代償として、ここまでやってこれた筈だ。

pages.en:
I swore it.

I made that vow to myself and resolved to become a Hero of Justice like Kiritsugu—like Dad.

Every year of Shirou Emiya's life existed for that alone.

I kept spending myself so that I might stand proudly before those who could not be saved. That bargain is what carried me this far.
pages.mirrorMoon:
…I swore never to let such a thing happen again.
I made an oath with myself to become a superhero like Kiritsugu.
Emiya Shirou’s days were turned to that sole purpose.
I let others use me so that I could hold my head up high before those who were not saved, and I made it this far because of that.

You know the cause.

You already know the enemy you must destroy.

The black sun.

If the shadow bored through the sky is responsible, you must kill it before this happens again.

Remember. What have you lived for all these years?

You justified your own existence by saving those who begged for salvation, by helping those innocently swept into disaster.

If you deny all that for the sake of one woman—

“—Right. Sakura, what would you like for breakfast?”

I place my hand upon Sakura, asleep beside me.

Strangely, I remember exactly why she is sleeping there.

Perhaps the girl I love sleeping beside me matters more than anything so trivial as who I am.

The fact that the girl I love is sleeping next to me is probably more important than my identity.

pages.en:
There is no one in the living room.

“H—ah—”

My body will not obey me. Trying to avoid the table, I slam my foot into it instead.

I fall, brace myself against the wall, somehow force myself upright, and stagger toward the hallway.

“—. —, —”

Am I panicking?

There is nothing wrong with my body, yet my mind refuses to settle.

Why am I panicking? What am I afraid of?

I try to put it into words, but whenever I begin to think deeply, I find myself in the world ten seconds later.

Am I unable to think?

Or do the thoughts simply fail to enter my awareness?

My newly awakened brain is so starved of blood that I cannot even tell the difference.

“Right. Tohsaka is the only one who went out, so Sakura must still be in the house.”

—Ah. That is why I felt relieved.

Sakura has not gone anywhere.

Good, good. My head is clearing at last.

It is obvious, really. Sakura must have woken before me and be washing her face, preparing breakfast, practicing in the dojo, or doing laundry in the garden.
